findings.title: Unconditional 5s cap overrides caller context, truncating long fetches
findings.recommendation: Honour the caller's deadline: only add the default cap when ctx carries no deadline (if _, ok := ctx.Deadline(); !ok { ... }), or make the timeout a parameter. With the current code a caller passing a 60s deadline gets its request cancelled at 5s and receives a context deadline exceeded error for a perfectly healthy server.

findings.title: Body silently truncated at 1 MiB with no error on oversize response
findings.recommendation: LimitReader returns EOF at the limit, so a 5 MiB response yields 1 MiB of valid-looking bytes and a nil error; the caller cannot tell the payload was cut. Read maxBody+1 bytes and return an explicit error when len(body) > maxBody, or expose the truncation to the caller.

findings.title: Nil client panics instead of returning an error
findings.recommendation: Guard with if client == nil { client = http.DefaultClient } (or return an error) so a nil argument produces a diagnosable failure rather than a nil-pointer panic that bypasses the returned-error contract of this function.

findings.title: Error status path discards body and does not drain it, preventing connection reuse
findings.recommendation: The status text is returned without the server's diagnostic body, which makes debugging 4xx/5xx calls hard; consider returning a typed error carrying StatusCode and a bounded snippet of the body (the deferred Close does drain on some transports, but only up to a small cap, so include the snippet explicitly).

findings.title: No tests for context cancellation, timeout, or oversize body

findings.recommendation: Add table tests using httptest: a pre-cancelled context must return a wrapped context error before dialling, a slow handler must hit the deadline, and an oversize body must exercise the limit path so the truncation behaviour is pinned down.
